findings.title: Task 1 fixture edits break existing tests, and the unindexed example never matches
findings.description:
- **The unindexed example can't match.** Task 1 suggests `7. [~] Feature Epsilon without explicit index — cut for scope.` with no `**…**` around the name. `PLAN_UNINDEXED_RE` (`packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/slicePlanParser.ts:9`) requires the bold name. The line would still be dropped after the regex change, so Task 5's unindexed assertion fails. The slice design's criterion uses `N. [~] **Name** — rationale`.
- **A bolded unindexed line still breaks things.** It would get fallback index 1 and sort first. That breaks the `entries[0]` (index 101) and `entries[2]` (index 103) assertions at `packages/core/tests/introspection/slicePlanParser.test.ts:12-30`. It also breaks the "every entry `indexSource: explicit`" test at `slicePlanParser.test.ts:126-129`.
- **Other tests that use this fixture break too.** `packages/core/tests/introspection/ArtifactIntrospector.test.ts:52` asserts `totalSlices` is 5. Task 5 only updates the length and totals test in `slicePlanParser.test.ts`.
- **Fix:** put both `[~]` forms in a new sibling fixture, which the slice design allows ("or add a sibling fixture"), and leave `sample-slice-plan.md` alone. The existing tests then prove the regression criterion unchanged. Task 5's edits to the existing totals test and its added "byte-identical regression" test can then be dropped.

findings.title: Task 8 misses the second `Pick` and wrongly describes the caller
findings.description: `resolveEntryStatus` is only called from `resolveEntryStatusSafe`, not with a full `SlicePlanEntry`. `resolveEntryStatusSafe` also declares `entry: Pick<SlicePlanEntry, 'index' | 'isChecked'>` (line 736). If only line 694 is widened, the call at line 740 won't type-check. Task 8 should say to widen both `Pick`s, and drop the claim that "its only caller passes a full SlicePlanEntry".

findings.title: Task 9's reason for changing the initializer is wrong, and the `degraded` path is not covered
findings.description:
- **The stated reason is wrong.** Task 9 says the initializer at line 91 is the value used if `detectDocuments` throws. It isn't: the `catch` at line 126 sets `derivedStatus = 'degraded'`, so whatever line 91 holds is overwritten. The edit is harmless but would mislead whoever implements it.
- **The real gap is not mentioned.** Lines 122-123 return `'degraded'` before `deriveEntryStatus` runs. A `[~]` entry with an unreadable task file or bad frontmatter therefore shows `degraded`, not `deprecated`. Decision 4 says a plan-line `[~]` is definitionally true regardless of what the task file or frontmatter says, so arguably it should win here too.
- **Fix:** replace the line-91 step with a decision on whether plan-line deprecated takes priority over `degraded` in `slice.ts` and in `resolveEntryStatusSafe`. If it does, add one test for it.

findings.title: `arch-status-vs-plans` has no test
findings.description: The criterion names both `plan-status-vs-entries` and `arch-status-vs-plans`. Task 12 only tests the first. Both read the same `completedSlices` value from the parser, so the risk is low. One more case, or an explicit note in Task 12 that this is covered transitively, would close the trace.

findings.title: Task 11's "stop and report to the Project Manager" step
findings.description: Project rules ignore steps that wait on the PM unless a named rule requires them. Saying "don't guess at a fix" fits the debugging rule, which is to get evidence first. The step could simply say to diagnose with the test output instead of stopping.
